audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings call Malphite's W 'Brutal Strikes' and credit it with stacking bonus armour. Riot's current text names it Thunderclap and gives it no armour at all — it is a sonic boom that makes his attacks create aftershocks. Granite Shield, a shield worth 10% of his max health that recharges when he goes unhit, is never mentioned once. Ground Slam is never named either, despite being a 7-second ability that reduces YOUR attack speed and deals damage scaling off his armour — the single hardest counter to Irelia's passive in his kit. The mirror audit (malphite__irelia) also established that Ionian Fervor is stacking attack speed plus on-hit damage with no resistance reduction anywhere; this page calls it 'armor shred' five times, including in the TL;DR.
audit.why: Two compounding errors: the reader is told to fear armour W does not give, and is told her passive shreds armour it does not shred — so she builds and trades on a stat model that does not exist. Meanwhile the two abilities that actually decide the lane (a recharging 10%-max-HP shield to force out, and an attack-speed cut on a 7s cooldown) are invisible.
audit.corrected: Thunderclap named correctly with aftershocks instead of armour; Granite Shield introduced as the thing to force out before committing; Ground Slam named with its 7s cooldown and attack-speed reduction; every 'shred' claim about Ionian Fervor removed, matching the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with the packet and the prose: Level 1 read Irelia while whys[0] tells you to concede and eat poke; Level 3 read Malphite while whys[2] calls it your one clean window; Levels 4-5 read Malphite while whys[3] says it depends on you; Level 6 read Irelia while whys[4] and spikes[2] both say Unstoppable Force knocks you out of your own combo.
audit.why: 45.05% over 1443 Emerald+ games is a losing lane with one real window at 3. The mirror audit independently proposed flipping Level 6 to Malphite, so leaving it as Irelia would have put the two pages in direct contradiction.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3 and 4 flipped in both layers as one atomic group with matching ratings, giving Malphite, Skill, Irelia, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite — identical to the packet and consistent with the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere despite the whole page being built on 'catch him after he spends Q'.
audit.why: Seismic Shard is a flat 8 seconds and Ground Slam a flat 7 — those two numbers are what make the level-3 window real or imaginary, and Unstoppable Force is 130s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam's 7s written into spikes[3] and wants.foe[1]; the Granite Shield recharge condition added as the other half of the timing in the full layer's win condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file marks Seismic Shard with a 'grounding' flag, which would matter enormously to a dash champion.
audit.why: Riot's description of Seismic Shard says only that it damages and steals movement speed for 3 seconds — no grounding. Treated as a tooltip-parsing misfire and not asserted either way.
audit.corrected: Nothing written about grounding. The slow is described as what it is.

edits.before: Malphite's Seismic Shard (Q) pokes and slows you, and the slow is the real problem — it drags you out of Bladesurge-reset range so you can never stick to him. At levels 1-2, farm with Q off the wave and eat the poke; do not walk up to auto into his Brutal Strikes (W), which hands him bonus armor and a cleaving empowered strike that out-trades your early hits. Your one early opening is level 3: if he wastes Q to shove, step in with your E (Flawless Duet) stun then Bladesurge-reset for a quick burst before his armor matters, then back off the slow.
edits.after: Malphite's Seismic Shard (Q) pokes and steals your move speed, and that is the real problem — it drags you out of Bladesurge-reset range so you can never stick to him. At levels 1-2, farm with Q off the wave and eat the poke; don't walk up into Thunderclap (W), whose aftershocks out-trade your early hits, and remember Granite Shield eats your first 10% of his health for free unless you keep hitting him. Your one opening is level 3: if he spends Q to shove, E-stun and Bladesurge-reset for a burst, then back off the slow.

edits.before: This is where it gets ugly. Malphite stacks armor on Brutal Strikes and his first armor item, and your whole kit — Bladesurge autos, passive on-hit, the armor shred from your stacks — leans physical, so your damage falls off a cliff into him. At 6 his R (Unstoppable Force) is point-and-click unstoppable: it knocks you up through your E-stun and dashes and sets up a free gank, and once you are airborne your reset engine does nothing. Only all-in if his Q is down AND his R is on cooldown; otherwise take this window to shove and roam, because you do not out-trade an armor-stacked Malphite on raw stats.
edits.after: This is where it gets ugly. Malphite buys armour and your whole kit — Bladesurge autos, Ionian Fervor on-hit — is physical, and Ground Slam cuts the attack speed those stacks are made of every 7 seconds, so your damage falls off a cliff into him. At 6 his R (Unstoppable Force) knocks you up straight through your E-stun and your dashes and sets up a free gank, and once you are airborne your reset engine does nothing at all. Only all-in if his Q is down AND his R is on cooldown; otherwise take the window to shove and roam, because you do not out-trade an armour-itemised Malphite on raw stats.

notes: Two errors compounded on this page. First, Malphite's W was called Brutal Strikes — a name Riot retired — and credited with stacking armour it does not grant; it is Thunderclap and it makes his attacks create aftershocks. Second, and confirmed by the malphite__irelia mirror, Ionian Fervor was called armour shred five times including in the TL;DR; Riot's text is stacking attack speed plus on-hit damage with no resistance reduction. Granite Shield (10% max health, recharges out of combat) and Ground Slam (7s, scales off his armour, cuts your attack speed) were both entirely absent and are the two abilities that actually decide the lane. Four chart rows flipped as a matched group, including Level 6 to Malphite, which is what the mirror audit also proposed.
